description:
Mozhaysk Elephants unites three students passionate about science and technology. Timofey focuses on programming, AI, math, physics and entrepreneurship. Kirill explores geography, space, satellite imagery and geospatial technologies. Evgeny develops multi-agent AI systems, business automation solutions and tech startups. Together, we combine AI, software and geospatial analysis to solve real-world challenges.

Our motto: Think big, explore beyond!
summary: ASTRA is a prototype health monitoring application for long space missions. A crew member manually records measurements, symptoms, and the conditions under which readings were taken, then reviews their personal history. The application displays changes over time and statistical forecasts for 24 hours, 72 hours, and seven days. A locally hosted AI assistant asks follow-up questions and explains available information using selected, source-linked knowledge cards. ASTRA also presents archived NASA radiation measurements from the ISS and laboratory records from NASA study OSD-575 in separate research views. After initial setup, the application can operate without an internet connection, supporting health review when communication with Earth is limited. ASTRA is a hackathon prototype and has not undergone clinical validation.
details:
During a long mission, a crew member may notice fatigue or a change in a health measurement. To understand what it means, they need their earlier readings, the conditions in which those readings were taken, and the context of the mission. ASTRA brings this information into one place. A user records a symptom or measurement, and the application shows that person’s history and how their readings have changed.

ASTRA’s distinctive idea is to connect the assistant’s conversation with personal measurements and mission context. The locally hosted AI assistant considers recent messages and relevant cards from a source-linked knowledge base. It asks follow-up questions, explains possible causes, and suggests a next step. Application code separately calculates statistical forecasts for 24 hours, 72 hours, and seven days with an uncertainty range. The crew can review the personal measurements behind a forecast and discuss a developing change early.

ASTRA also presents 84 archived ISS radiation environment readings and 532 laboratory records from NASA study OSD-575, with links to their sources. These research data appear separately from crew records. After initial setup, ASTRA runs locally, which matters when communication with Earth is limited. We built the interface with React and TypeScript, the API with Python and FastAPI, and local storage with SQLite. Qwen3:8b runs through Ollama. Measurements are entered manually in the current prototype. Sensor integration and clinical validation are the next development stages.
